description.narrative: Severe Tropical Cyclone (TC) Lola hit Vanuatu’s Northern and Central provinces from 24 - 25 October 2023 as a Category 5 cyclone, impacting over an estimated 57,000 people and causing widespread damage to infrastructure, houses and crops. It also caused damage in Temotu Province in the Solomon Islands. This investment is Australia's immediate response to the cyclone and includes support for the Vanuatu Government's response efforts including humanitarian relief supplies and funding for NGOs under the Australian Humanitarian Partnership to deliver targeted humanitarian assistance to impacted communities. The current estimated value of this investment is $850k from the Humanitarian Emergency Fund to be expensed from Oct 2023 - Oct 2024. $800k funding is for the Vanuatu's Government's response and $50k is for the Solomon Island Government's response.

description.narrative: Tropical Cyclone Lola struck Vanuatu’s northern and central islands on 24 and 25 October 2023. It was the third cyclone in eight months to cross Vanuatu following Tropical Cyclones Judy and Kevin in March 2023, which impacted many of the same communities. Australia was quick to respond, with lifesaving emergency supplies distributed to 50,145 people through local authorities and CSOs. Emergency supplies allowed communities to drink clean water, maintain basic hygiene, and conduct emergency repairs to their homes in the immediate aftermath of the devastating cyclone. Australia continued to support affected communities into the recovery phase through infrastructure repair and reconstruction, replacement of medical equipment and school curriculum materials, and by helping farmers get agricultural systems up and running again.
